text.name: TextDesc2
text.text: The TRS-80 MC-10 was a compact home computer introduced by Tandy Corporation in 1983 as an inexpensive entry-level system for home users and beginners. Powered by a Motorola MC6803 processor, it included 4 KB of RAM, Microsoft Color BASIC in ROM, and used standard cassette tapes for software storage. The MC-10 shared its Motorola MC6847 video hardware with the TRS-80 Color Computer, allowing colorful graphics despite its modest specifications. Designed to compete with low-cost home computers such as the Sinclair ZX81 and Commodore VIC-20, the MC-10 emphasized affordability and ease of programming. Although its limited memory restricted more advanced software, it gained popularity among hobbyists and students and remains a distinctive member of the TRS-80 family.
